items.headline: Thompson Twins Make NBA History with Blockbuster Extensions, Duren's Standoff Continues
items.summary: Ausar Thompson and Amen Thompson have become the first brothers in NBA history to each sign contracts worth over $100 million, securing combined deals totaling $363 million. Ausar secured a monster extension with the Pistons, while Amen landed a huge new deal with the Rockets. This comes as their teammate, Jalen Duren, is reportedly holding out on a five-year, $200 million offer from Detroit, with rival teams reportedly circling the All-NBA big man.

items.headline: Doc Rivers Retires from Coaching, Joins NBC as Analyst
items.summary: After a storied coaching career, Doc Rivers has officially announced his retirement from coaching and will be joining NBC as a game analyst for the upcoming 2026-27 NBA season. Rivers, 64, brings over four decades of NBA experience and was inducted into the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame earlier this year.

items.headline: Nicolas Batum Announces Retirement After 18-Year NBA Career
items.summary: Veteran forward Nicolas Batum has officially retired from the NBA after an 18-season career. Batum shared the news in a social media video with his son, citing a desire to spend more time with family.

items.headline: Clippers Hit with Heavy Penalties in Salary Cap Scandal
items.summary: The NBA announced on September 2 that the Los Angeles Clippers have been stripped of five first-round draft picks (2029-2033) and fined $30 million for salary cap circumvention. Owner Steve Ballmer has also been suspended from league and team activities for one year.

items.headline: Kawhi Leonard Traded to Toronto Raptors
items.summary: The Toronto Raptors have acquired two-time Finals MVP Kawhi Leonard from the Los Angeles Clippers. In exchange, the Clippers received Brandon Ingram, Gradey Dick, two unprotected first-round picks, a first-round swap, and two second-rounders.

items.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo Headed to Miami Heat in Blockbuster Deal
items.summary: Two-time MVP Giannis Antetokounmpo has been traded to the Miami Heat along with Bobby Portis, concluding a year-long saga. The Milwaukee Bucks received Tyler Herro, Kel'el Ware, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kasparas Jakučionis, the No. 13 pick in the 2026 draft, first-round picks in 2031 and 2033, and a 2030 pick swap and 2033 second-round pick.

items.headline: Clippers Bolster Roster with Draft Picks and Trades
items.summary: The LA Clippers had a busy offseason, acquiring Keaton Wagler (No. 5 pick), Baba Miller (36th), Nick Martinelli (55th), and Narcisse Ngoy (57th) in the 2026 NBA Draft. Earlier, they traded James Harden to CLE for Darius Garland and a second-round pick and sent Ivica Zubac and Kobe Brown to IND for Bennedict Mathurin, Isaiah Jackson, two first-round picks, and a second-rounder. They also acquired Max Strus from CLE and traded John Collins to DET.

items.headline: Paul George Traded to Celtics; Julius Randle to Nets
items.summary: Paul George has been traded from the Philadelphia 76ers to the Boston Celtics in exchange for Jaylen Brown and multiple draft picks. Additionally, Julius Randle was moved from the Minnesota Timberwolves to the Brooklyn Nets in a three-team deal involving the Chicago Bulls.

items.headline: LaMelo Ball Traded to Timberwolves in Multi-Player Deal
items.summary: LaMelo Ball has been traded from the Charlotte Hornets to the Minnesota Timberwolves. As part of the multi-team deal, Josh Green also joined Minnesota, while the Hornets received Naz Reid, Matteo Spagnolo, and several draft picks.

items.headline: LeBron James Signs with Philadelphia 76ers
items.summary: Four-time NBA champion LeBron James has signed with the Philadelphia 76ers as a free agent, making one of the biggest moves of the offseason.

items.headline: Lakers Make Splash with Walker Kessler Signing
items.summary: The Los Angeles Lakers kicked off free agency with a major acquisition, signing Walker Kessler to a four-year, $130 million deal. The Lakers also added Quentin Grimes, Collin Sexton, and Sandro Mamukelashvili.

items.headline: Rui Hachimura, Bradley Beal Re-sign with Clippers
items.summary: The Los Angeles Clippers have re-signed forward Rui Hachimura to a two-year, $28 million deal, and veteran guard Bradley Beal to a two-year, $13.2 million contract. Jordan Miller and Kobe Sanders also re-signed with the team.

items.headline: Tobias Harris Joins San Antonio Spurs
items.summary: The San Antonio Spurs addressed their forward depth by signing veteran Tobias Harris to a two-year deal worth over $15 million annually.

items.headline: Mitchell Robinson to Celtics, Marcus Smart to Rockets
items.summary: Center Mitchell Robinson has joined the Boston Celtics on a three-year, $47.4 million contract. Meanwhile, guard Marcus Smart signed a two-year, $13 million deal with the Houston Rockets.

items.headline: Coby White Returns to Charlotte Hornets
items.summary: Guard Coby White has re-signed with the Charlotte Hornets, maintaining a key backcourt presence for the team.

items.headline: NBA Training Camps Set to Open September 29
items.summary: Teams across the league are preparing for the official start of training camps, which are scheduled to open on September 29, marking the final roster-building stage before the preseason.

items.headline: Numerous Coaching Changes Highlight Offseason Moves
items.summary: The 2026 offseason saw a flurry of coaching changes: Taylor Jenkins replaced Doc Rivers in Milwaukee, Tiago Splitter took over for Billy Donovan in Chicago, Jamahl Mosley moved from Orlando to New Orleans with Sean Sweeney taking the Magic job, Dusty May succeeded Jason Kidd in Dallas, and Micah Nori was hired by Portland. Brian Keefe was also named the Washington Wizards' head coach.

items.headline: 2026-27 NBA Regular Season Schedule Released
items.summary: The NBA released the full regular-season schedule on August 13, with the season officially tipping off on October 20, 2026. Preseason games are slated to run from October 3-11.

items.headline: International Games Announced for 2027
items.summary: The NBA plans to host two regular-season games in Europe in January 2027, with the San Antonio Spurs facing the New Orleans Pelicans in Paris, France on January 14 and in Manchester, United Kingdom on January 17.

items.headline: Wizards' Trae Young Praises Top Draft Pick A.J. Dybantsa
items.summary: Washington Wizards star Trae Young has high praise for the team's top draft pick, A.J. Dybantsa, calling him 'cold' and 'the real deal,' generating excitement for the upcoming season.
